V primeru skupne ponudbe lahko pogoj partnerji izpolnijo skupaj. V primeru, da ponudnik nastopa s podizvajalci, lahko pogoj ponudnik in podizvajalci dokazujejo skupno. DOKAZILO: - V primeru izpolnjevanja pogoja iz prve alineje prvega odstavka te točke: Izpolnjen obrazec P- 10 Referenca ponudnika. Referenca mora biti potrjena s strani naročnika referenčnega posla s podpisom. V kolikor se referenca nanaša na naročnika (Ministrstvo za zunanje in evropske zadeve), ponudnik izpolni vse podatke, vendar podpis reference s strani naročnika ni potreben. - V primeru izpolnjevanja pogoja iz druge alineje prvega odstavka te točke: ustrezna navedba v točki 3 obrazca P-2 Prijava in dokazila o izkušnjah ter sodelovanju strokovnjaka (npr. pogodba o zaposlitvi). 9.4.2 Vsi kadri ponudnika, ki bodo opravljali dela predmetnega javnega naročila, bodo varnostno preverjeni s strani naročnika v skladu z 16a. členom Zakona o zunanjih zadevah (Uradni list RS št. 113/03– uradno prečiščeno besedilo, s spremembami in dopolnitvami, v nadaljevanju ZZZ-1). STATEMENT OF WORK C. 1. OVERVIEW/BACKGROUND. The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory

The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory of NLS DA2 devices. NLS requires quantities suffi

C.2 BACKGROUND NLS administers a free program that loans audio and braille books and magazines, music scores in braille and large print, and specially designed audio-playback and refreshable-braille-display equipment to residents of the United States who are unable to read or use standard print materials due to visual or physical impairment. NLS administers the program nationally, while direct service to eligible individuals and institutions is the responsibility of cooperating network libraries in the various states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, Guam, and the U. S. Virgin Islands. This service is also extended to eligible American citizens residing abroad. The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of the Director, Office of Acquisitions, intends to negotiate and award a ﬁrm-ﬁxed-price purchase order on a non-competitive basis to Xact Metal, Inc., 200 Innovation Blvd, Ste 257, State College, PA 16803 for one (1) Advanced Metal Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) 3D Printing System, including required software, accessories, installation, and on-site operator training, in support of the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI), Division of Intramural Research. Market research conducted in accordance with FAR Part 10 concluded that the Xact Metal XM200-series LPBF platform is the only commercially available system that simultaneously satisﬁes all of the Government's mandatory salient characteristics — including qualiﬁed processing of titanium alloys, copper, and stainless steel on a single multi-material platform; feature precision of 50 microns or ﬁner; an integrated glovebox for safe handling of reactive metal powders; single-phase 100–240 VAC laboratory power compatibi

monly used engineering metals; • Multi-material capability supporting a range of metal powders without fundamental system modiﬁcation; • Integrated system for safe handling of reactive metal powders, including titanium, through an enclosed or controlled environment (e.g., glovebox or equivalent); • Compact footprint suitable for installation and operation within a biomedical research laboratory; • Compatibility with standard single-phase laboratory electrical infrastructure (100– 240 VAC, 50–60 Hz); • Inclusion of all required software, accessories, and operational components necessary for full system functionality; • Provision of on-site installation and operator training. The system shall be delivered, installed, and made fully operational within sixty (60) days after contract award. Installation and training shall be coordinated with the Government technical point of contact.
